{"status": "answered", "answer": "Under the Card Dispute Procedure (Rev 5), the process works as follows:

**Form:** You'll complete Form HCU-DSP-114 (Card Transaction Dispute) when you report the dispute.

**Provisional Credit:** For debit cards, provisional credit is posted within 10 business days of the dispute notice if the investigation hasn't finished by then (or within 20 business days if your account is less than 30 days old). For credit cards, the disputed amount is suspended from your balance instead of providing provisional credit.

**Investigation Timeline:** The investigation takes up to 45 calendar days, or up to 90 calendar days for point-of-sale transactions, foreign transactions, or accounts less than 30 days old.

**Outcome Notification:** Card Services notifies you in writing within 3 business days of completing the investigation. If the dispute is in your favor, any provisional credit becomes final. If no error is found, the notice explains the findings and when the provisional credit will be reversed (at least 5 business days after the notice).", "cited_chunk_ids": ["card_dispute_procedure::layout::B_structure::0001", "card_dispute_procedure::layout::B_structure::0003", "card_dispute_procedure::layout::B_structure::0004", "card_dispute_procedure::layout::B_structure::0005"], "reason": "All four elements of the question—the form used, provisional credit timing, investigation duration, and outcome notification—are fully answered in the provided passages from the Card Dispute Procedure Rev 5."}
